sections.title: How rendering works

blocks.title: Not from your PDFs
blocks.text: Your PDFs do not cover this topic, so this page was written for the site. Your 12-week plan lists React, hooks, rendering, performance, state management and TypeScript. Check it against the official documentation, or give me a PDF to replace it.

blocks: "Rendering" means React calling your component function. It does not mean updating the DOM. React then compares the result and touches only what changed, so a render with no changes is usually cheap.

blocks.title: From state change to screen
blocks.code:
flowchart LR A[setState] --> B[Render phase
call the components, compare trees] B --> C[Commit phase
apply DOM changes] C --> D[Browser paints] D --> E[Effects run]
blocks.caption: The render phase can be repeated or discarded, so it must have no side effects.

blocks: A component re-renders when **its state changes, its parent re-renders, or a context it uses changes**. Props changing is not the trigger: by default a child re-renders whenever its parent does, even with identical props.

blocks.title: Together they let a row skip re-rendering

walkthrough.title: memo
walkthrough.text: Skips re-rendering when all props are shallowly equal.

walkthrough.title: useMemo
walkthrough.text: Caches a calculated value until its dependencies change.

walkthrough.title: useCallback
walkthrough.text: A new arrow function on each render would defeat `memo`, so the function is kept stable.

blocks.title: Measure first
blocks.text: Use the React DevTools Profiler to find what is slow before adding these. They have a cost and do nothing unless the child is memoised or the calculation is expensive. The React Compiler can add this memoisation automatically in projects that enable it.

rows: Typing in an input re-renders a whole page
Move the state down into the component that uses it
A list of thousands of rows
Virtualise it (TanStack Virtual, react-window): render only visible rows
Typing lags behind a heavy filtered list
`useDeferredValue` or `useTransition` to mark the update as low priority
Use stable keys; do not define components inside components

blocks.title: Gotcha
blocks.text: Defining a component inside another component creates a new type on every render, so React unmounts and remounts it and its state is lost. Define components at the top level.

blocks.title: Interview angle
blocks.text: **A page is slow. What do you do?** Reproduce it in a production build, record with the React DevTools Profiler, and find which components render and why. Then move state down first, virtualise long lists, split bundles, and add `memo` only where the profile shows a benefit.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
- Render means calling the function, not updating the DOM.
- A parent re-rendering re-renders its children by default.
- Moving state down is usually the best fix.
- `memo` needs stable props, hence `useCallback` and `useMemo`.
- Measure with the Profiler, in a production build.

items.question: Does a child re-render if its props did not change?
items.answer: Yes, when its parent re-renders, unless it is wrapped in `memo`.

items.question: Why doesn't `memo` help when you pass `onClick={() => ...}`?
items.answer: A new function is created on every render, so the prop always differs. Use `useCallback`.

items.question: You must show 50,000 rows. What do you do?
items.answer: Virtualise: render only the visible rows and reuse them while scrolling.

items.question: Why must rendering have no side effects?
items.answer: React may call a component several times or discard a render, so side effects could run repeatedly or for output never shown.
